findings.title: Sandboxed (Flatpak) apps reach the IME through org.freedesktop.portal.Fcitx and can flip and probe the global VI/EN mode; threat model residual-risk text is outdated
findings.scenario: fe-fcitx owns org.freedesktop.portal.Fcitx. xdg-dbus-proxy lets every Flatpak app talk to org.freedesktop.portal.* by default, and its uid equals the user's, so peer_allowed() passes. The app calls CreateInputContext, then ProcessKeyEvent with Control_L/Shift_L press+release on its own IC (no FocusIn needed): ime.rs:336 toggles the one global mode for every app on both routes. The same app can learn the current mode (send 'a','a' and see whether the preedit is 'â') and watch when the user toggles. No text of another context leaks: contexts are per sender (contexts.rs), signals are unicast (server.rs emit_signal with destination), and the IBus socket is not visible in the sandbox. The impact is integrity of the mode only (e.g. a password typed in a field without a content purpose gets Telex-composed). But 02_threat-model.md:91 still says Flatpak apps get no Vietnamese input unless an IBus portal is added, so this sandbox-facing surface was never threat-modelled.
findings.fix_hint: Update the threat model and README residual risks: the fcitx portal is the sandbox entry point, it exposes only InputMethod1/InputContext1 with the SEC-9/SEC-12 checks, and any sandboxed app can change the global mode. Optional hardening: in ime-core, count a Ctrl+Shift tap only on a context that has received FocusIn and no FocusOut since (a `focused` flag in Context), so a background or sandboxed client cannot flip the mode.

findings.title: README does not list any of the accepted residual risks and wrongly says XIM is served (SEC-14 'limitation is in the README' not met)
findings.scenario: The threat model's 'Residual risks (accepted, documented in README)' section and SEC-14's check ('reviewer checks the limitation is in the README') both need README text. README.md is 18 lines and says 'not usable yet'. It still says the binary serves XIM, which D19 dropped (fe-xim is a stub that returns Ok at once). It does not mention: same-user X11 keylogging; text on the fcitx route crossing the session bus, where any unconfined same-user process can monitor or eavesdrop as with stock fcitx5; Flatpak access through the fcitx portal; D25b (text left in zbus buffers); D22 (a word in progress is lost when the daemon crashes); the recovery command. A user who reads the README to judge the keystroke exposure gets no answer.
findings.fix_hint: Add a 'Security and known limits' section with the residual risks above, the recovery path (systemctl --user disable --now vr-talex.service, then ./uninstall.sh), and the D25a/D26/D17 limits. Drop XIM from the feature line.
